candidate.rationale: The only effect is consuming the linear read token and updating a private atomic reader count; neither produces a public logical result.
risks: Exposing the hidden count would break abstraction and be unstable under concurrency.

candidate.rationale: The semantic effect is consumption of the linear ReadHandle, already enforced by taking self by value. The remaining mutation is private concurrent state; any public ensures would either expose unstable internals or merely repeat facts known before the call.
risks: The release effect remains represented by linear ownership rather than an explicit postcondition.
A future public ghost model of reader ownership would require revisiting this decision.
